key_insight: ThoughtTrace is the first large-scale dataset that links real-world multi-turn human–AI conversations with users' self-reported thoughts (reasons for prompts and reactions), exposing the latent intent and judgments that are absent from standard dialogue corpora.
problem_solved: Existing conversational datasets record only utterances, not users' internal motivations or reactions, limiting progress on intent inference, evaluation, personalization, and alignment of LLMs with real user goals.
method: Collected paired data from 1,058 real users: 2,155 multi-turn conversations and 17,058 turns, yielding 10,174 self-reported thought annotations across 20 language models.
Annotated each turn with users' explicit reasons for sending prompts and their reactions to assistant responses, creating aligned conversation–thought pairs.
Performed dataset analyses to characterize thought types, distribution across LMs, and implications for modeling user intent and feedback-informed training.
impact: Provides a new supervision signal for training and evaluating models that must infer intent, predict user satisfaction, or personalize responses; enables better alignment and safety by making latent user reasoning observable.
visual_elements: Dataset composition card: large numeric icons showing 1,058 users | 2,155 conversations | 17,058 turns | 10,174 thought annotations | 20 LMs
Paired interaction diagram: side-by-side timeline of a conversation turn and the corresponding user 'thought' bubble (reason + reaction)
Thought-type distribution chart: stacked bar or pie chart showing proportions of common thought categories (e.g., goal, clarification, emotion, correction)
Modeling pipeline schematic: how ThoughtTrace can be used for intent inference, feedback-conditioned response tuning, and evaluation
paper_title: ThoughtTrace: Understanding User Thoughts in Real-World LLM Interactions
paper_authors: Chuanyang Jin, Binze Li, Haopeng Xie, Cathy Mengying Fang, Tianjian Li
